key_insight: Rice husk ash can be converted into silica powder that is amorphous after 800 °C treatment and becomes crystalline quartz/cristobalite after annealing at 1200 °C.
engineering_relevance: This creates a low-cost silica feedstock with tunable phase structure for thermal spray powder development and coating applications.
method: Chemically treated rice husk ash to extract SiO2
Heat treated the product at 800 °C for 3 h to form amorphous silica
Annealed at 1200 °C to induce crystallization; characterized by XRD, FTIR, and laser diffraction
evidence_signal: XRD confirmed amorphous silica after initial processing and identified quartz and cristobalite after 1200 °C annealing, while laser diffraction gave a D50 of about 88.9 μm.
watch_item: The powder’s relatively large particle size and the phase change at high temperature may affect flowability, deposition behavior, and coating consistency in thermal spray systems.
paper_title: Synthesis of Amorphous and Crystalline Silicon Dioxide Powder Composites from Rice Husk Ash for Thermal Spray Deposit
